## Proof

Let $f \in L^2[-\pi,\pi]$, and define the Fourier coefficients

$$
c_n \;=\; \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} f(x)\,e^{-inx}\,dx,\qquad n\in\mathbb Z.
$$

The hypothesis states that $\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} f(x)\,e^{-inx}\,dx = 0$ for every integer $n$, i.e. $c_n = 0$ for all $n\in\mathbb Z$.

By the **Plancherel (Parseval) theorem** for the orthonormal system $\left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{inx}\right\}_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ of $L^2[-\pi,\pi]$, every $f\in L^2[-\pi,\pi]$ satisfies

$$
\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} |f(x)|^2\,dx \;=\; 2\pi\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} |c_n|^2.
$$

Since $c_n = 0$ for every $n$, the right-hand side vanishes:

$$
\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} |f(x)|^2\,dx \;=\; 2\pi\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z} 0 \;=\; 0.
$$

(Note: $|f|^2 \ge 0$ a.e., so a zero integral also forces $f=0$ a.e., consistent with the completeness of the trigonometric system.)

$$
\boxed{\displaystyle \int_{-\pi}^{\pi} |f(x)|^2\,dx \;=\; 0}
$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
